verdicts.reason: A keeps the logo, headline and CTA in a sensible left column, but the phone has shrunk and been pulled out of its circle and photo panel. That leaves the photo panel as a large empty brown box and makes the product a tiny afterthought. B is worse: the headline and CTA sit on the circle, which is cut off at the right edge, the left half is a blank blurred photo, and the phone is a thumbnail stuck in the bottom gutter, so the product is effectively gone.

In A the phone is a decent size and the text column reads clearly. But the phone only half-overlaps the circle, which sits inside an inset photo rectangle that is now an empty, purposeless block on the right. The tiny logo is also not aligned with the headline's left edge. B has the same failures as pair 1 B: an empty photo half, text crammed onto a circle cut off at the edge, and a tiny phone, so the product imagery is lost.
